{{Short description|Statistic in epidemiology}}
In [[epidemiology]], the '''attack rate''' is the proportion of an at-risk population that contracts the disease during a specified time interval.<ref name=lesson3 >{{cite web |date=10 December 2019 |title=Principles of Epidemiology Lesson 3 - Section 2 |url=https://www.cdc.gov/csels/dsepd/ss1978/lesson3/section2.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417064836/https://www.cdc.gov/csels/dsepd/ss1978/lesson3/section2.html |archive-date=17 April 2020 |accessdate=7 April 2020 |website=Centers for Disease Control and Prevention}}</ref> It is used in hypothetical predictions and during actual [[outbreaks]] of disease. An at-risk population is defined as one that has no immunity to the attacking pathogen, which can be either a [[novel pathogen]] or an established pathogen. It is used to project the number of infections to expect during an [[epidemic]]. This aids in marshalling resources for delivery of medical care as well as production of vaccines and/or anti-viral and anti-bacterial medicines.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Glaser |first=Anthony N. |title=High-Yield Biostatistics |date=April 1, 1995 |publisher=Williams & Wilkins |isbn=978-0-683-03566-7 |location=Baltimore}}</ref>

The rate is arrived at by taking the number of new cases in the population at risk and dividing by the number of persons at risk in the population.<ref name=lesson3 />

{{center|<math>\mbox{attack rate} = \frac{\mbox{number of new cases in the population at risk}}{\mbox{number of persons at risk in the population}}</math>}}
